# LazyAPI

> OpenAPI-driven API testing from the terminal. The OpenAPI spec is the source of truth; tests are JavaScript/TypeScript files next to it (linked per operation with `x-lazyapi-tests`). Every exchange is checked: request matches the spec, status is declared, response matches the schema, and the script's test() calls pass.

## Validate an API (agent loop)

1. `lazyapi list ops <spec> --json` — operations (operationId, method, path, tags, tests file)
2. `lazyapi describe <spec> <operationId> --json` — parameters with examples, request/response schemas, referenced components
3. `lazyapi send request <spec> --op <operationId> [--param k=v] [--body @file] --output json` — one call with all checks and the full response
4. Write `.lazyapi/tests/<operationId>.js` and set `x-lazyapi-tests` (or MCP `write_test`)
5. `lazyapi run <spec> --output json` — exit 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 usage error, 3 could not run

Scenarios across operations: write `.lazyapi/flows/<name>.js` (lazyapi.send in order + test()); run with `lazyapi run <spec> --flow .lazyapi/flows/<name>.js` or `--flows`. Every step is checked against the spec. A test script may `export function before(req)` to change the request (auth, signatures) before it is sent, and `export function after(res)` to clean up what it created (runs even when tests fail). Data-driven: `lazyapi run <spec> --data rows.csv|json` runs once per row with the row's values in env ({{env.col}}); MCP run_tests data_file. `lazyapi.send("GET https://host/users/42")` maps a URL to its spec operation. Postman: `lazyapi import postman <collection> --environment <env.json> --into api.yml` (pm.* scripts incl. pm.sendRequest keep working). Named environments (server, env file, vars, credentials incl. OAuth2) live in .lazyapi/config.yml: `--env-name staging`.

Import: `lazyapi import curl|postman|har <source> --into <spec>` (Postman scripts are translated to test/expect/env; untranslatable lines are marked TODO(postman)). Export: `lazyapi send request <spec> --op <id> --output curl`. Forms: `--form k=v`, `--file name=path`. TLS/proxy: `--insecure`, `--ca-cert`, `--client-cert/--client-key`, `--proxy`, or `http:` in .lazyapi/config.yml.

No server yet? `lazyapi mock <spec>` serves the examples on http://127.0.0.1:4010 and validates requests (422). `Prefer: code=404` selects a declared response.

Large responses: `send --jq '<filter>'` (CLI) or the `jq` argument of send_request (MCP) returns only that slice of the body.
MCP: `lazyapi mcp --root <dir>` exposes list_specs, list_operations, describe_operation, send_request, run_tests, run_flow, write_flow, read_test, write_test, validate_spec, script_api, import_curl, export_curl.

## Docs

- [Agents and MCP](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/agents): setup, tools, five-step loop
- [Test scripts](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/scripting): globals, matchers, imports, lockfile
- [run](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/cli/run): selection, parallelism, JSON report format
- [send](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/cli/send): single requests
- [mock](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/cli/mock): fake API from the spec
- [Environments & Auth](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/environments): .lazyapi/config.yml, credentials, OAuth2
- [describe / validate](https://githiago-f.github.io/lazyapi/latest/cli/inspect)
- Script API types: run `lazyapi types`
- Fake data: {{$randomEmail}}, {{$guid}}, … in requests (new value per occurrence; `lazyapi fake` lists them), `faker.*` in scripts; a test script's exported functions are dynamic values too (`export function randomSku()` → {{$randomSku}}, overrides built-ins)

## Rules of thumb

- `run` only sends GET/HEAD/OPTIONS unless `--methods all`.
- Path params come from `--param` or spec examples; missing values skip (run) or fail (send) — never invented.
- Imports: relative files inside the spec dir, or `https://` URLs (pinned in .lazyapi/lazyapi.lock; use `--frozen-lockfile` in CI). Bare names like `zod` are rejected — use `https://esm.sh/zod@<version>`.
- Scripts are synchronous; `lazyapi.send()` returns the response directly.
